Q19_core_contributions: Phenomenon & metrics: reference-induced instability definition with corrected variance decomposition (V_ref, V_ref_frac), tail-risk metrics (CVaR_0.1, CVaR_0.2, CFR, best-worst gap), prediction consistency (J_pred, MAD_ref). Phase S V_ref bug fixed.
Unified reference-resampling protocol: patient-disjoint, k in {1,3,6}, 10 seeds, 3 prompt configs, shared across datasets, frozen before holdout.
Confirmatory benchmark on unseen MoNuSAC holdout (n=40): 10/10 WP1 gate conditions pass.
Cross-dataset evidence: MoNuSeg STRONG_SUPPORT (9/9); IDRID FAIL - establishes instability is real/predictable but mean-consensus mitigation is dataset-dependent, NOT universal.
Strong deterministic baseline: B2 Mean Consensus k=6 improves Dice +0.0266, CVaR +0.0276, CFR -0.0058 on MoNuSAC holdout, with 1 SAM call.

Risk-aware mitigation: M2 dual-model selective prediction (separate instability + catastrophic models) - AUROC 0.94 val / 0.93 holdout, AUPRC 0.43 val / 0.53 holdout, CFR reduction 39.2% val / 79.2% holdout at 80% coverage. Dual-model design necessary because labels are anti-correlated.
Failure taxonomy: 4 modes - small-sparse-target, diffuse-map, prompt-interface, reference-catastrophic.
Negative results: M1 dynamic budget NO_GAIN (CV selects zero penalties); Phase S learned weighting does not beat uniform mean (-0.0024 Dice).
